A standard pin tumbler lock consists of the shell, the plug, the shear line, and the pin stacks each containing a spring, a driver pin, and a key pin. The defeat relies on exploiting microscopic imperfections created during manufacturing called machining tolerance. Applying slight rotational force to the plug causes it to bind against the single most misaligned pin stack called the binding pin. Lockpicking systematically exploits this by applying tension with a tension tool, lifting the binding pin to the shear line where the plug rotates a tiny fraction trapping the driver pin above the shear line, then transferring binding to the next misaligned pin and repeating until all driver pins are trapped and the plug rotates freely.
